svg.title: Medicare and Medicaid Billing Fraud Reporting Gates
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-medicare-billing-reporting-gates; chapter number: 5; chart type: decision_tree; title: Medicare and Medicaid Billing Fraud Reporting Gates; subtitle: Four checks before an insider files a False Claims Act case; caption: Systemic provider fraud proven with knowing conduct pays 15 to 30 percent; intervened cases average about $13M against about $3M declined, so speed and clean evidence matter.; assumptions note: Gate order is a sequencing of the operator gates quoted by the cited practitioners; settlement averages are Brown's generalized statistics, not case guarantees.; note: Sources: Brown, LLC (Jason T. Brown, faQOCnnY-QI, nDO81fwnTqg, 7two8gR6AAY), Stephen Teller - Teller Law (0w534uBbqVQ), Baker Donelson (Tom Barnard, -Vss5I_7dHM).; nodes: gate: G1; question: Is the target systemic billing fraud by a provider rather than a neighbor misusing benefits?; pass next: G2; fail action: Report directly to the government; individual benefit cases are not the qui tam lane (Brown, LLC).; gate: G2; question: Can you show knowing conduct, including reckless disregard or deliberate ignorance, with emails or firsthand facts?; pass next: G3; fail action: A nurse disagreeing with medical necessity is a tough case to make; keep documenting (Teller).; gate: G3; question: Is every billing statement, email, or medical record one you are lawfully entitled to access?; pass next: G4; fail action: Stop gathering and call whistleblower counsel first to avoid termination or criminal exposure (Brown, LLC).; gate: G4; question: Are you clear of signing, profiting, or handing over a Medicare number?; pass next: File fast with counsel; only the first to file has rights (Brown, LLC; Barnard).; fail action: Assume personal exposure and raise it with counsel before any report (Brown, LLC).

text.title: Medicare and Medicaid Billing Fraud Reporting Gates
text.tspan: Medicare and Medicaid Billing Fraud Reporting Gates

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Is the target systemic billing fraud by a provider rather than a neighbor misusing benefits?; pass next: G2; fail action: Report directly to the government; individual benefit cases are not the qui tam lane (Brown, LLC).

gate: G2; question: Can you show knowing conduct, including reckless disregard or deliberate ignorance, with emails or firsthand facts?; pass next: G3; fail action: A nurse disagreeing with medical necessity is a tough case to make; keep documenting (Teller).

gate: G3; question: Is every billing statement, email, or medical record one you are lawfully entitled to access?; pass next: G4; fail action: Stop gathering and call whistleblower counsel first to avoid termination or criminal exposure (Brown, LLC).

gate: G4; question: Are you clear of signing, profiting, or handing over a Medicare number?; pass next: File fast with counsel; only the first to file has rights (Brown, LLC; Barnard).; fail action: Assume personal exposure and raise it with counsel before any report (Brown, LLC).

text.title: Assumptions: Gate order is a sequencing of the operator gates quoted by the cited practitioners; settlement averages are Brown's generalized statistics, not case guarantees.
text.tspan: Assumptions: Gate order is a sequencing of the operator gates quoted by the cited practitioners; settlement averages are Brown's
